messages.subject: problem with ordered factors
parts:
Dear all,

in my simple SEM model I have two exogenous categorical variables (V1 and V2), and four endogenous continuous variables (R1 : R4). The models structure looks like:

> model<-'
R1 ~ V1 + V2
R2 ~ V1 + V2
R3 ~ V1 + V2

R4 ~ R1 + R2 + R3 + V1 + V2

#and the covariances:
R1 ~~ R2
R1 ~~ R3
'

When I run
> fit.sem <- sem(model,data=data,meanstructure=TRUE,test="satorra.bentler")

I get the following error:

> In getDataFull(data = data, group = group, group.label = group.label,  :
lavaan WARNING: unordered factor(s) detected in data: V1 V2

Or:
> Erro em vnames(FLAT, type = "ov.x", ov.x.fatal = TRUE) :
lavaan ERROR: model syntax contains variance/covariance/intercept formulas
involving (an) exogenous variable(s): [exogenous1 exogenous2];
Please remove them and try again.

when I included "ordered=c("V1","V2)"

What do these error messages mean? Could you please explain me what mistakes I might be making?

Thank you very much for your help,
André

messages.subject: Re: problem with ordered factors
parts:
On 03/14/2013 11:56 PM, andref...@yahoo.com.br wrote:
> Dear all,
>
> in my simple SEM model I have two exogenous categorical variables (V1
> and V2), and four endogenous continuous variables (R1 : R4). The models
> structure looks like:
>
> > model<-'
> R1 ~ V1 + V2
> R2 ~ V1 + V2
> R3 ~ V1 + V2
>
> R4 ~ R1 + R2 + R3 + V1 + V2
>
> #and the covariances:
> R1 ~~ R2
> R1 ~~ R3
> '
>
> When I run
> > fit.sem <- sem(model,data=data,meanstructure=TRUE,test="satorra.bentler")
>
> I get the following error:
>
> > In getDataFull(data = data, group = group, group.label = group.label, :
> lavaan WARNING: unordered factor(s) detected in data: V1 V2

Note that this is a warning, not an error. The warning tells you that
you have two (exogenous) variables in your model (V1 and V2) which in
the data.frame 'data' are marked as 'factor'. lavaan (unlike, say, lm())
currently does not automatically expand categorical predictors to a set
of dummy variables. You have to do that yourself. Hence the warning.

> Or:
> > Erro em vnames(FLAT, type = "ov.x", ov.x.fatal = TRUE) :
> lavaan ERROR: model syntax contains variance/covariance/intercept formulas
> involving (an) exogenous variable(s): [exogenous1 exogenous2];
> Please remove them and try again.

Exogenous variables should be declared as 'ordered'. Only dependent
variables.

Yves.
